items.description: The default scan never enters a reparse target, following is opt-in only, and the depth budget reports too_deep.
items.pass_condition: Without -Follow every reparse point is registered but not entered (Skipped counts all six); with -Follow a target that closes an ancestor cycle is reported as 'cycle' and a target that cannot be resolved or does not exist is reported as 'broken_target'; a directory already at -MaxDepth is reported as 'too_deep' instead of being enumerated.
items.failure_reason: The walker descends into reparse targets by default, follow mode silently enters a cyclic or dangling target without reporting it, or the depth limit is silently applied without the documented 'too_deep' diagnostic.

items.description: In-scope is decided on directory boundaries, not on a raw string prefix, and the root is inside itself.
items.pass_condition: A reparse target that merely shares a leading name with the scan root (scanroot-extra vs scanroot) is reported InScope = false, while a target genuinely nested in the scan root is InScope = true; a path equal to the root is inside it.
items.failure_reason: Containment is tested with a substring prefix, so sibling directories whose names begin with the root name are treated as inside, or the root itself is excluded.

items.description: A relative reparse target is resolved against the directory that contains the link, and canonical paths keep their casing and volume-root shape without a trailing separator.
items.pass_condition: For 'link-rel' (raw target 'docs') the resolved target is <scanroot>\docs; Get-WReparseCanonicalPath returns the input path with its original casing, preserves a volume root such as 'C:\', and drops any trailing separator.
items.failure_reason: A relative target is resolved against the process working directory, canonicalisation lower-cases the path, or it mangles volume roots and trailing separators.

items.description: Entry kind is decided by the reparse file attribute; hard links are ordinary files, link flavours stay distinguishable, and record fields follow the contract.
items.pass_condition: A hard link is reported with Kind = 'File'; a junction is reported with ReparseKind = 'Junction' and a symbolic link with ReparseKind = 'SymbolicLink'; the report carries SchemaVersion 'wreparse/1.0'; directories and reparse entries report Size = 0; a reparse entry records its raw on-disk target verbatim.
items.failure_reason: Any entry that exposes a link type is treated as a reparse point, so hard links are misclassified, junction and symbolic link collapse into one value, non-file entries report a non-zero size, or the raw target is normalised before being recorded.

items.description: Ordinary files and directories are enumerated with the documented depth convention.
items.pass_condition: Plain files and directories appear with the correct Kind, and every direct child of the scan root - including a reparse entry - is reported with Depth = 1.
items.failure_reason: Entries are skipped, given the wrong Kind, or depth is off by one for plain entries or for reparse entries.

items.description: The report is ordered by the contract comparison and contains no volatile values.
items.pass_condition: Record paths are non-decreasing under ordinal-ignore-case with an ordinal tie-break, the error list is sorted the same way (RelativePath then Code), and two consecutive reports of the same tree serialise to identical JSON.
items.failure_reason: Records or errors keep enumeration order, or the report embeds a timestamp and therefore differs between runs.

items.description: Statistics partition records into exactly one of the three kinds.
items.pass_condition: Stats.Directories, Stats.Files and Stats.ReparsePoints each equal the number of records of the matching Kind.
items.failure_reason: Reparse points are folded into the directory count.

items.description: Structural problems with the scan root are reported with the documented error codes.
items.pass_condition: A missing scan root yields a 'not_found' error and a file scan root yields a 'structure' error.
items.failure_reason: Structural failures are swallowed or reported with an undocumented code.
